Residences at new London project St John's Wood Square for sale, priced from GBP5.3 mil
article:
Savills Singapore is introducing St John’s Wood Square, a luxury residential development on the site of the former St John’s Wood Barracks in northwest London, to buyers in Singapore.

Prices start from GBP5.25 million (about $9 million) for a two-bedroom residence, the firm said in a Nov 17 release.

The development will have 120 residences, including single-level apartments, duplexes, penthouses and townhouses. The homes have an average size of over 3,260 sq ft.

Sales launched in October, and completion is phased from spring 2028 to 1Q2029.

The project’s site was previously used as military barracks for the King’s Troop and the Royal Horse Artillery. In 2012, the 5.5 acre (2.2ha) plot was purchased by the late Malaysian billionaire Ananda Krishnan for GBP250 million. Krishnan, who founded business ventures including Malaysian telco Maxis and media company Astro Malaysia Holdins, died in 2024.

According to Savills, the development is now led by George Iacobescu, the project’s executive chairman and former chairman and CEO of Canary Wharf Group.

The project will include 2.6 acres of landscaped gardens and about 40,000 sq ft of private residents’ amenities. The centrepiece is The Riding Club, a members’ club in the restored Riding School, a Grade II-listed building built in 1825.

Amenities include a 20m swimming pool, spa and wellness facilities, sports courts, private dining areas, a cinema and children’s play spaces.

The development is located near The Regent’s Park, Primrose Hill, Marylebone and London’s West End. The St John’s Wood area is known for its green spaces, independent shops and proximity to international schools.

Iacobescu said the aim was to create “residences that respect and complement their surroundings, while delivering an unrivalled level of craftsmanship, comfort and quality”.

Noting that Krishnan envisioned “a meaningful long-term retention” of the project, he added that the developer will oversee the estate’s ongoing operation as its “long-term custodians”.

Adrian Lim, head of international residential sales at Savills Singapore, said London continues to appeal to Singapore-based buyers looking for established neighbourhoods with long-term value.

He said the project offers “a rare combination of heritage, exclusivity and contemporary luxury”.

title: CapitaLand-Far East Organization-Sing Holdings consortium tops Town Hall Link tender with $1.82 bil bid
article:
The Government Land Sales (GLS) tender for a white site at Town Hall Link in Jurong Lake District (JLD) closed on Nov 17, attracting two bids. A consortium comprising CapitaLand Development , Far East Organization and Sing Holdings submitted the highest offer of over $1.82 billion, or $910 psf per plot ratio (ppr).

The consortium's bid was 38.9% higher than the second bid of over $1.31 billion ($655 psf ppr) submitted by Sim Lian Group .

The 99-year leasehold site is expected to yield up to 1,200 private residential units, alongside office, retail and other commercial uses. Located within JLD, the development will help transform the area into Singapore's largest mixed-use business district outside the city centre.

The Town Hall Link site was launched for tender on July 3. Spanning 400,719 sq ft, it has a maximum gross floor area (GFA) of about 2 million sq ft.

The development must include at least 40,000 sqm (430,556 sq ft) of office space and between 20,000 sqm and 44,000 sqm of retail space. Other permitted uses include serviced apartments, hotels, recreational and community facilities.

In a joint statement, CapitaLand Development, Far East Organization and Sing Holdings say the site's scale, mixed-use potential and connectivity to Jurong East MRT interchange and the future Cross Island Line station align with their expertise in developing large integrated urban projects.

“We see an opportunity to create a vibrant live-work-play destination at JLD, as Singapore’s largest mixed-use business node outside the city centre,” the consortium says.

Limited bids for large mixed-use site

The nearly 39% gap between the two bids suggests developers differ in their assessment of the value that can be extracted from the site, says Leonard Tay, head of research at Knight Frank Singapore.

Wong Siew Ying, head of research and content at PropNex, says the two bids were not unexpected, given the substantial capital commitment required for a development of this scale.

Since 2021, the 10 GLS sites sold for at least $1 billion have attracted an average of about three bids, with two sites drawing just one bid each, she notes.

Such tenders tend to appeal to a smaller pool of well-capitalised developers and consortiums, particularly when mixed-use projects require expertise across residential, office and retail development, Wong adds.

While the site's strategic location and transport connectivity are attractive, developers would have weighed these advantages against the substantial execution risks associated with a large integrated development, says Knight Frank's Tay.

In particular, the mandatory office component poses a challenge at a time when "the popularity of suburban office facilities remains untested", he adds.

Smaller site, higher land rate

The Town Hall Link site forms part of the original 6.5ha JLD master developer site, which was launched for tender in June 2023.

When the tender closed in March 2024, it attracted two concept proposals from a single consortium comprising CapitaLand Development, City Developments Ltd (CDL) , Frasers Property , Mitsubishi Estate and Mitsui Fudosan .

However, URA decided not to award the site in September 2024, as the shortlisted proposal's bid of about $2.5 billion, or $640 psf ppr, was deemed too low.

Following the unsuccessful tender, URA scaled down the development opportunity to about half the original maximum GFA to make it more accessible to a broader pool of developers.

Mohan Sandrasegeran, head of research and data analytics at SRI, says the revised site configuration will allow developers to pursue a "more focused development strategy".

PropNex's Wong notes that the Government will also undertake more infrastructure and land preparation works for the area south of Jurong Town Hall Road, potentially reducing development costs for the successful tenderer.

The smaller site and reduced infrastructure obligations may have lowered bidders' capital commitments and development risks, supporting a higher land rate this time, she adds. However, Wong cautions that the two sites are not directly comparable.

The latest top bid of $910 psf ppr is 42.2% higher than the $640 psf ppr offered for the original master developer site in 2024.

Nevertheless, Knight Frank's Tay says it remains uncertain whether the Government will award the site, as the latest bid could still fall short of its reserve price.

However, Mark Yip, CEO of Huttons Asia, believes the Government should award the site to kick-start JLD's development.

He considers the latest bid fair, noting that the land rate is significantly higher than that offered in 2024, despite relatively unchanged conditions in the suburban office and retail markets.

While office demand remains relatively weak, residential prices have risen significantly over the same period, Yip adds.

Potential record for white site outside Central Area

CapitaLand Development, which was part of the original five-member consortium in 2024, has now returned with Far East Organization and Sing Holdings, submitting the highest bid for the smaller Town Hall Link site.

Yip also notes that the $1.82 billion bid is likely to set a record as the highest land price by quantum for a white site outside the Central Area.

For comparison, the last white site sold in the Jurong East Planning Area was acquired for $969 million ($1,012 psf ppr) in May 2011.

The site has since been developed into Westgate, a mixed-use development comprising a seven-storey retail mall and a 20-storey Grade-A office tower linked to Jurong East MRT interchange.

Meanwhile, the white site now occupied by IOI Central Boulevard Towers in the CBD attracted seven bids when its tender closed in November 2016. IOI Properties Group secured the site for $2.57 billion ($1,689 psf ppr).

"Buyers and investors remain highly attracted to transit-oriented integrated sites," says Yip.

The Town Hall Link development will have an underground connection to the future Jurong Lake District MRT station on the Cross Island Line, as well as an elevated pedestrian bridge linking it to Jurong East MRT interchange, which serves the North-South and East-West lines and will eventually connect to the Jurong Region Line.

The site is also close to established shopping malls, including JEM , Westgate and IMM, providing future residents with convenient access to retail, dining and other amenities, says Marcus Chu, CEO of ERA Singapore.

Commercial and residential opportunities

Upon full completion, JLD is expected to accommodate 100,000 new jobs and 20,000 new homes, strengthening its position as a major employment and residential hub in western Singapore.

The substantial office component at Town Hall Link will support the area's development as a decentralised commercial hub, while its future office population could drive demand for homes and retail amenities within the integrated development.

According to Huttons Data Analytics, Singapore's office supply pipeline is projected to peak in 2028 before tapering off over the following three years, potentially reducing future supply risks for developers.

Other major projects planned for JLD include the new Science Centre Singapore, slated to open by end-2027, and Jurong Gateway Hub, an integrated development expected to be completed in 2029.

Residential prices could average above $2,800 psf

The Town Hall Link site is also close to two 99-year leasehold private residential developments in Jurong Gateway: the 738-unit J Gateway , launched in June 2013, and the 368-unit J'den , launched a decade later in November 2023.

J Gateway was nearly sold out on its first day of launch, with units sold in the first month averaging $1,466 psf, based on caveats lodged. Completed in 2016, the development has seen 26 resale transactions so far this year, averaging $2,092 psf.

Meanwhile, J'den sold 88% of its units on its launch weekend at an average price of $2,451 psf. The nine units sold so far this year have averaged $2,545 psf, bringing total sales at the project to 98.5%, based on caveats lodged.

The most recent GLS site awarded in the wider Jurong area was at Lakeside Drive, which CDL secured in June 2025 for $607 million, or $1,132 psf ppr.

The site is being developed into the 570-unit Lucerne Grand, which was launched on the first weekend of October 2026. The project saw 350 units (61.4%) sold during its launch weekend at an average price of $2,480 psf.

Based on caveats lodged to date, Lucerne Grand is 72.6% sold at an average price of $2,489 psf.

PropNex's Wong expects the residential component of the Town Hall Link development to attract healthy interest from HDB upgraders in the west and buyers drawn to its connectivity and proximity to schools.

She estimates that new apartments at the development could achieve an average selling price above $2,800 psf, supported by its integrated mixed-use concept, future access to four MRT lines and JLD's ongoing transformation.

title: Executive condo prices likely to remain stable, developers may sell around 1,800 new units in 2027: Huttons
article:
Prices of executive condos (ECs), a hybrid public-private housing class, are likely to hold steady next year while up to 1,995 new units from five projects could be launched for sale, according to Huttons Asia’s forecasts.

Housing developers may also sell between 1,500 and 1,800 EC units in 2027.

The real estate agency noted a potential surge in demand in the coming year from both first- and second-time buyers who are keen to avoid the tighter EC policies.

The new restrictions on the EC market — which include a longer minimum occupation period (MOP) and the removal of the deferred payment scheme (DPS) — as well as the higher income ceiling of $18,000 are expected to apply to projects launched from 2028 onwards.

Explore comprehensive data about all ECs , including the average profit at 5 and 10 years

In the meantime, the five upcoming launches slated for 2027 will remain under the previous policy framework.

“Furthermore, the number of HDB flats fulfilling their five-year MOP will increase by 40.5% y-o-y in 2027 to 18,939 units, significantly increasing the available pool of second-time buyers,” said Huttons on Nov 17.

It added that although higher interest rates are likely in 2027, buyers of new EC units can still opt for DPS then to manage their mortgage instalments.

Forecast launches and sales of EC projects in 2026 and 2027:

Upcoming launches next year include the 430-unit Wynwood Grand and 570-unit Clovelle of Woodlands, both situated along Woodlands Drive 17; the 300-unit Solano Grand on Senja Close; the 265-unit Fablewoode Residences on Sembawang Road; and the 452-unit Miltonia Close in Yishun.

In 2026, average prices for new EC projects climbed past the $1,900 psf benchmark. This came after they had exceeded $1,700 psf in 2025.

Two EC developments were launched this year: Coastal Cabana in January and Rivelle Tampines in March. In total, 1,320 new EC units were offered for sale, similar to 2025.

Huttons on Nov 17 noted that Coastal Cabana has sold more than 85% of its homes at a median price of $1,800 psf. It is the first EC project in 12 years in Jalan Loyang Besar and also features sea views.

Meanwhile, Rivelle Tampines has moved almost 98% of its units at a median price of $1,934 psf. Likely the last EC project in the east in 2026 and 2027, it is next to a mixed-use development linked to Tampines West MRT Station.

Overall, Huttons estimated that a total of 1,500 new EC units would be sold for the whole of this year, slightly below 2025’s sales volume of 1,630 units.

“Extending a trend since 2023 of sales outpacing new launches, these figures underscore strong market demand for affordable private housing,” Huttons wrote.

In particular, new EC units continue to have a “strong pricing advantage” over new private non-landed homes situated in the Outside Central Region (OCR) or suburbs, the agency added.

The median price quantum for ECs this year stood at $1.826 million, roughly 26% lower than that of OCR private condos. In terms of psf prices, the median for ECs was $1,846 psf, which represents a 21% discount.

title: S$10,000 in DBS Shares: How Much Dividend Income Could You Receive in 2027?
article:
DBS Group Holdings Ltd
(SGX: D05) has long been a local favourite among Singapore investors seeking reliable dividend income.
The group’s popularity stems from its strong banking franchise, consistent profitability and track record of rewarding shareholders.
However, if you had S$10,000 to invest today, how much dividend income could DBS realistically generate in 2027?
In this article, we will examine the numbers and whether the bank’s current valuation makes it an attractive income investment.
How Many DBS Shares Can S$10,000 Buy?
On 6 November 2026, DBS shares closed at S$69.72.
With S$10,000, investors could purchase 140 shares.
This amounts to 14 board lots of 10 shares each, following Singapore Exchange’s reduction of DBS’s board lot size in October 2026.
At this price, the investment would cost S$9,760.80 before brokerage fees.
Assuming a S$10 brokerage fee, investors would have S$229.20 remaining.
Importantly, a higher share price means fewer shares for the same investment.
Had shares been bought at a lower price, the yield on cost would be higher, assuming dividends remain unchanged.
How Much Dividend Income Could DBS Pay in 2027?
DBS has progressively increased its ordinary dividends.
Recently, the bank declared S$0.66 per share for each quarter from 1Q2026 to 3Q2026.
Annualising these quarterly payments gives an ordinary dividend of S$2.64 per share.
Separately, DBS introduced a Capital Return dividend of S$0.15 per share quarterly in 2025, which management plans to maintain through 2027.
This represents another S$0.60 per share annually, although these additional dividends should not be treated as permanent recurring dividends beyond the announced period.
Assuming investors hold 140 DBS shares throughout 2027 and receive four quarterly payments, here are three potential scenarios.

*Includes the S$0.60 annual Capital Return dividend.
Under the base case, investors would receive S$369.60 in ordinary dividends and S$84 in Capital Return dividends, bringing total annual income to S$453.60.
This annual income works out to a monthly equivalent of approximately S$37.80.
The conservative scenario assumes ordinary dividends decline amid weaker earnings.
Meanwhile, the optimistic scenario assumes a further increase supported by stronger profitability.
Can DBS Sustain Its Dividend Payments?
DBS’s latest quarterly results showed
some pressure
, but overall earnings were resilient.
In the third quarter of 2026 (3Q2026), total income fell 1% year on year (YoY) to S$5.85 billion, while net profit declined 5% to S$2.81 billion.
The picture was slightly better when looking at the first nine months of 2026 (9M2026), with net profit rising 2% YoY to S$8.82 billion.
For 9M2026, net interest income slipped 1% YoY to S$10.79 billion as lower Singapore interest rates were largely offset by loan growth and hedging.
In 3Q2026 alone, net interest income rose 4% YoY.
Meanwhile, its wealth management business continued to grow strongly.
For 9M2026, wealth management fees grew 24% YoY to S$2.69 billion, contributing to a 15% YoY increase in net
fee income
to S$4.37 billion.
In addition, DBS reported a Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio of 15.9% as at 20 September 2026.
With annualised earnings per share of S$4.15 for 9M2026 and an annualised ordinary dividend of S$2.64, DBS’s payout ratio works out to approximately 63.6%.
This provides some comfort for income investors, as loan growth and asset quality remained healthy in 9M2026.
However, lower interest rates, slower loan growth or higher credit costs could still put pressure on future earnings.
Is DBS Still Worth Buying for Dividend Income?
At S$69.72 per share, DBS’s annualised ordinary dividend of S$2.64 gives a yield of approximately 3.8%.
The inclusion of the planned Capital Return dividend would also increase the prospective 2027 yield to about 4.6%.
However, investors must recognise that this higher yield includes a time-limited payout.
At S$69.72 per share, DBS trades at around 2.85 times its net book value of S$24.47 per share as at 30 September 2026.
This multiple is known as the price-to-book (P/B) ratio.
The premium reflects DBS’s strong profitability, with return on equity reaching 17% for 9M2026.
However, its relatively high valuation also means that a slowdown in earnings growth could weigh on its share price.
Furthermore, investors should consider the risks of putting nearly all their S$10,000 into a single bank.
If investors spread their capital across different companies and sectors, it could help reduce their exposure to DBS’s performance.
Get Smart: How Much Can S$10,000 in DBS Really Earn?
Based on its current dividend payments and planned capital returns, having a S$10,000 investment in DBS could generate between S$420 and S$487 in dividend income in 2027.
The base case estimate of S$454 annually appears reasonable given DBS’s resilient earnings, capital position and current ordinary dividend level.
However, investors should note that the capital return dividend is only planned through 2027 and ordinary dividends are dependent on future profitability.
Ultimately, DBS is an appealing dividend stock, but its relatively high valuation means investors should weigh income received against potential capital losses.
A
reliable dividend
is valuable, but paying the right price for that income matters just as much.

title: Deluge secures $18.5 mil in new contracts, order book reaches $459.1 mil
article:
Deluge Corporation Limited (Deluge) announced that it has secured approximately $18.5 million in new contracts across both Singapore and Malaysia. With the latest contract win, Deluge’s outstanding order book has reached $459.1 million.

The new contracts secured span across infrastructure, marine and offshore, residential and industrial projects, which includes a data centre project in Penang, Malaysia.

In particular, Deluge states that the Penang data centre project is targeted for completion by March 31, 2027 and is expected to contribute positively to its financial performance for FY2027 ending March 31, which subjects to project progress and revenue recognition.

“Beyond growing our order book, our priority is to maintain strong execution while building a sustainable pipeline of opportunities to support long-term growth,” says Lee Wai Wah, executive director and CEO of Deluge.

Shares of Deluge closed 0.5 cents lower, or down 0.82% at 60.5 cents on Nov 17.

title: Geo Energy confirms no new mining directive received in latest clarification statement
article:
Geo Energy Resources, on Nov 17, confirms that its mining operations in Indonesia remain operational as usual and the group has not received any notice on new regulation, ministerial decree or implementing guidelines.

The latest clarification statement comes as recent media reports covers the remarks made by Indonesian President, Prabowo Subianto on Nov 14, regarding the government’s intention to secure a share of at least 70% of the benefits from all mining permits and if necessary, hold controlling stakes in mining assets.

Based on Geo Energy’s assessment of its existing fiscal contributions, the group has been contributing to the Indonesian government in excess of 70% of its profit through corporate income taxes, mining royalties and other applicable fees payable under the prevailing regulatory framework.

“Furthermore, the board also notes that President Prabowo had indicated that the relevant mechanisms had already been implemented, rather than referring to entirely new requirements yet to be introduced,” Geo Energy adds.

The group also confirms that its existing mining business permits (IUPs) remain valid and in effect.

“The IUPs for PT Tanah Bumbu Resources and PT Triaryani (TRA) are valid until Jan 10, 2028 and May 22, 2030 respectively, extendable twice by up to 10 years at the option of the group,” Geo Energy elaborates.

See also: Airwallex plans over $2 bil Singapore investment to support global growth

Nonetheless, Geo Energy states that it remains on track to achieve its coal volume target of at least 11.5 million tonnes for 2026. The group has attained coal production of 7.2 million tonnes in 9MFY2026.

Geo Energy says that it will make further announcements on this matter if and when there are further developments.

Shares of Geo Energy were last traded at 38 cents back on Nov 16 when the group calls for a trading halt.

title: UK backs push to explore global levies on climate polluters
article:
(Nov 17): The UK is among nations championing a push to add new levies on polluting sectors of the global economy and direct the proceeds to bolster funding to manage the impacts of climate change.

A declaration launched Tuesday at the COP31 climate talks acknowledged the potential for “small levies” to help mobilise climate finance for developing countries. Other nations backing the initiative include Spain, Kenya and Timor-Leste, the document said, confirming an earlier report by Bloomberg News.

The UK will continue to advance the proposals into 2027, when it will hold the presidency of the Group of 20 nations. Timor-Leste is chair of the Least Developed Countries negotiating bloc under the United Nations, which includes 44 economies.

Solidarity levies typically refer to surcharges on business class travel, financial transactions and fossil fuel production. The individual levies often raise only small amounts of revenue, though they are seen as an important tool to widen the pool of financing directed toward climate action.

“We recognise the potential of innovative approaches to complement existing sources of public and private finance,” the declaration said, urging a shift from “repeated and incremental crisis response to one of sustained and transformational resilience-building and proactive financing to match the scale of this challenge.”

Tuvalu, Vanuatu and South Sudan are also supporting the initiative, the declaration said.

See also: Strong on form, short on returns

The issue of securing adequate flows of finance to tackle global warming — and to adapt to its impacts — is the subject of fresh debate at the UN-convened COP31 climate summit in the coastal resort city of Antalya, Türkiye.

For adaptation alone, international public finance from developed to developing countries reached about US$32 billion in 2024 and compares to an estimated annual need of US$305 billion by 2035, according to the UN Environment Programme.

Developed countries, along with the European Union, have made clear at the Antalya talks that they will not commit to fresh climate finance commitments, meaning that other sources could have to make up the shortfall.

See also: EU close to deal to link UK carbon market after Brexit split

Earlier this month, Brazil published a road map on how to scale climate finance to US$1.3 trillion by 2035, which included the prospect of raising about US$129 billion a year through so-called solidarity levies.

“We welcome the potential of targeted, small levies to ensure a contribution to the costs of climate action from polluting sectors and to mobilise more finance without adding to the sovereign debt burden,” the declaration said.

Almost US$200 million a year could be raised for climate finance by adding a US$60 to US$90 levy on premium airfares for flights arriving in 10 climate-vulnerable countries, the Global Solidarity Levies Task Force said in a report last week.

In an early draft of a COP31 decision text published Monday — one that is expected to be substantially revised in the coming days — the summit’s presidency included references to “innovative sources” of finance.

Last week at the talks, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for additional taxes on fossil fuel companies to pay for the damage caused by climate change. A group of nine major producers had reported collective profits of US$95 billion in the last quarter — many multiples higher than funding available to respond to climate disasters, he said.

“Part of that should go into adaptation and loss and damage funds,” said Jennifer Morgan, a former German special envoy for climate.

title: Japan to launch natural disaster warning network across Asia
article:
(Nov 17): Japan will create a network across the Asia-Pacific region to promote development of early-warning systems aimed at bolstering protections against extreme weather events and natural disasters.

Gaps in capabilities such as remote sensing and cell phone alerts have been highlighted by recent events, including the devastating August floods near the Nepal-China border, which killed more than 1,400 people and wiped out towns, border posts and hydropower plants.

“The network will share knowledge and expertise in the introduction and operation of the early warning systems and promote effective deployment,” Japan’s Environment Minister Hiroyoshi Sasagawa said Tuesday (Nov 17) in a speech to the COP31 conference in Antalya, Türkiye.

Japan, which lies on an arc of volcanoes and fault lines surrounding the Pacific Basin known as the “Ring of Fire", has been a pioneer in earthquake early-warning systems and developing buildings designed to withstand powerful tremors.

The country also remains committed to supporting countries with climate finance, though it sees a need for other nations to contribute more, Sasagawa said.

“To meet the needs of countries requiring support, it is essential to broaden the contributor base to include countries capable of contributing and to expand various financial flows including private finance,” he said at the conference.

See also: Japan’s GPIF fund keeps quarterly asset allocation little changed

Developed economies have persistently called for the likes of China, Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states to expand their climate finance contributions, while those nations argue that most responsibility should rest with countries that industrialised first.

title: US gas pump price hits lowest since March as oil supply recovers
article:
(Nov 17): US gasoline pump prices fell to the lowest since March following a broader decline in oil markets this month.

National regular unleaded gasoline dropped to an average of US$3.78 a gallon, according to the American Automobile Association. Global oil prices have fallen in recent weeks on increased flows from the Persian Gulf and indications from US President Donald Trump that he will hold off on renewed attacks against Iran.

While the move lower will be a welcome relief to US consumers, pump prices remain well above prewar levels.

title: Turkey fund assets shrink by US$54 bil amid manipulation probe
article:
(Nov 17): Türkiye’s asset-management industry shrank by the equivalent of US$54 billion in the two months through October as authorities investigated alleged market manipulation involving investment funds.

Assets under management fell about 17% to 13.14 trillion liras in October from 15.85 trillion liras in August, according to data from the Turkish Capital Markets Association.

The bulk of the contraction came in September, when the crisis erupted after Türkiye's capital-markets regulator ordered the liquidation of 131 funds managed by seven firms amid investigations into alleged manipulation of thinly traded stocks.

The seven managers’ combined assets plunged 85% to 281.7 billion liras in September, according to the data.

Türkiye's largest private banks meanwhile emerged from the turmoil with a bigger market share. The asset-management units of Isbank, Akbank, Garanti BBVA and Yapi Kredi now control 47.4% of the industry’s assets, up from 40.5% in August, as other managers bore the brunt of the losses.

The four firms collectively lost 188 billion liras over the two months, a decline of just 2.9%. Their combined assets rebounded by around 181 billion liras in October even as the broader industry continued to shrink.

See also: Dubai, Abu Dhabi investors’ options shrink on IPO slump, buyouts

Changes in assets under management reflect not only investor withdrawals but also fluctuations in market valuations and fund liquidations.

title: Nato turns to commercial rockets for greater space access
article:
(Nov 17): The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is contracting commercial rockets and spaceports to grow its satellite-launch network and help neutralise risks to the space systems on which it relies.

The alliance on Tuesday (Nov 17) launched its Starlift initiative, through which participating countries can secure slots on commercial rockets at spaceports across Nato countries and South Korea, deputy secretary general Radmila Shekerinska said at the opening of the Nato Edge technology conference in Izmir, Turkey.

The initiative is part of a Nato push to adopt more commercial technologies, with the alliance poised to offer more than US$3 billion in new private contracts in the next two years.

The expanded use of commercial launch providers and spaceports is intended to make Nato’s access to space more resilient and allow it to respond more quickly to threats, according to the alliance. Nato says its space systems — which support communications, navigation, intelligence and missile defence — face risks including cyberattacks and signal jamming.

Starlift will act as a launch brokerage platform, pooling military demand and matching it to commercial launch providers. It will also prepare and test procedures for short-notice launches, as might be needed during a crisis, according to Nato.

Ten members states — Belgium, Canada, Finland, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Turkey and the UK — along with South Korea have committed to financing Starlift through the Nato Support and Procurement Agency.

See also: Baidu’s Robin Li says AI needs monetisation to avoid bubble risk

Nato’s technology agency plans to offer about €2.7 billion in private contracts over the next two years, including to commercial space companies, Dylan Browne, general manager of the Nato Communications and Information Agency, said Monday. Other contracts will be for cloud, artificial intelligence, cyber, command-and-control and networks systems, Browne added.

“Nato must work with industry not only when a requirement has been finalised, but earlier,” Browne said. “We’ve got to work closer, with a clearer understanding of what the alliance needs next.”

Nato designated space as an operational domain in 2019 and has said attacks to, from or within space could lead to the invocation of its Article 5 collective-defence clause.

title: Indosuez Wealth Management and INSEAD prepare heirs to better manage family business
article:
Indosuez Wealth Management (WM) has launched the Asian edition of Indosuez Academy, a programme which equips future business leaders with the skills to navigate the challenges and opportunities unique to family businesses.

Inaugurated in 2025 at the INSEAD Europe Campus in Fontainebleau, France, the academy’s first edition in Asia was held at INSEAD’s Asia campus in Singapore from Oct 26-29. Participants include children and grandchildren of the bank’s clients from around the world, including Asia Pacific, Middle East, Europe and America.

The programme, designed in collaboration with INSEAD, offers a unique platform for business heirs to expand their knowledge, connect with global peers, and embrace their future roles with clear purpose, says Indosuez deputy CEO Mathieu Ferragut. “For over 150 years, Indosuez has guided global families through complex cross-generational transitions,” he adds. “Bringing together a diverse 2026 cohort from multiple countries, this programme is designed to cultivate strong stewardship and entrepreneurial vision.”

The curriculum will equip participants with resilient leadership, crisis communication, and governance skills to balance legacy preservation with strategic growth and innovation.

Laurent Proutière, Indosuez WM CEO for Asia, says: “As Asia undergoes a massive intergenerational wealth transfer, the academy’s launch in our region is very timely. Business founders are increasingly focused on succession planning, and Indosuez is committed to supporting this next generation of leaders.”

Antoine Duvauchelle, programme director, INSEAD, believes that the programme provided a “safe space” for the participants to have their assumptions challenged, learn from each other and reflect on how they lead and make decisions. “It has been gratifying to observe how they are taking on board these learnings and evaluating what can be applied to their own business and family context as they prepare for the responsibilities that come with taking over the reins,” he concludes.

title: Shanghai Exchange intervenes after historic copper crunch
article:
(Nov 17): The Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) has stepped in to try to ease an historic copper squeeze, as an acute shortage of available metal threatens to drain inventories.

Contracts for November delivery, which expired on Monday, soared to trade at a premium of over 14,000 yuan (US$2,100 or $2,707) a ton to contracts for delivery in December.

The dramatic spike on Monday came after on-warrant inventories had fallen to a level lower than open interest, raising the risk that more traders would request delivery than there was metal available to deliver.

To avoid that possibility, the SHFE pressured holders of long and short positions to settle them financially, according to people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be named as they weren’t authorised to speak publicly. While that achieved the desired effect of reducing open interest, it meant that short position holders were forced to buy back their positions, exacerbating the squeeze.

On-warrant stocks had fallen to just 2,270 tons last Friday, while open interest in the November contract stood at 4,810 lots, or 24,050 tons. SHFE had been encouraging holders of long positions to roll their positions rather than take delivery for several weeks, some of the people said.

See also: Aluminium squeeze intensifies with traders scrambling for metal

In early trading on Tuesday, the spread between December and January contracts widened, indicating that the squeeze may not be over.

Jia Zheng, a trading manager at Suzhou Chuangyuan Harmony-Win Capital Management Co, said that the tightness could persist until the end of the year. “Producers are holding back sales betting on spot premiums to continue rising, leaving buyers struggling,” she said.

See also: China’s US$17 bil crop pledge falters ahead of Trump-Xi summit

The squeeze is one of the most dramatic in the history of the copper market. The peak backwardation on the SHFE on Monday was twice that seen in a similar expiry squeeze on the London Metal Exchange (LME) in 2021, when the one-month backwardation flared out to as much as US$1,060 a ton.

It is also the latest in a series of short squeezes to hit metals markets, which have been left vulnerable by a drawdown in inventories caused by a variety of supply and trade upheavals ranging from US tariffs to the war in Iran. The LME copper market is also tight, while the LME aluminium market is in the grip of the biggest squeeze since the 1980s.

The Chinese copper market more broadly has tightened dramatically in recent weeks, with deliverable inventories falling to the lowest since 2023 and the premium for front-month contracts over later-dated months surging to the highest since 2005 — a condition known as backwardation that is indicative of short supply.

At the same time, physical premiums for copper — which are paid over and above the exchange price — have also jumped in China to trade at more than US$250 a ton, the highest in at least a decade. Bloomberg reported earlier that Trafigura Group had been buying large volumes of copper to boost sales into Asia, adding to a scramble for metal in the region.

The squeeze on supplies comes after copper flows were redirected away from China in the past two years, as traders rushed to ship metal to the US ahead of threatened tariffs. It also coincides with Asia Copper Week, as hundreds of miners and traders are descending on Shanghai to negotiate supply deals for the coming year with Chinese customers.

“Cathode is going to where the highest price is being paid, and that you know for now is Asia,” Nicholas Snowdon, Mercuria Energy Group’s head of metals and mining research, said at an industry conference in Shanghai on Tuesday. “Term premiums will in general be higher this year than last year, and the appetite for volume and long-term contract is much stronger than it was last year.”
